George and nursery - a relatively new Royal tradition

Prince George is continuing a royal tradition, but not one that is long established.

The Queen was educated at home and relied on her nanny, Crawfie, to take her on educational trips - including a journey on the London tube.

Prince Charles did go to school, but his nursery was a palace room containing a blackboard, a desk and a governess.

It was at his mother's insistence that Prince William was exposed to children of his own age when he started at Mrs Mynors' school.

webpage.text:
Prince George Will Be Attending Nursery School Starting in January

Imagine driving your child to nursery school in the morning and seeing, in the car behind you, Kate Middleton in the driver’s seat, handing George a backpack and a folder of loose papers, giving him a kiss before he jumps out of the car. Imagine showing up to a bowling birthday party, to find Prince William feeding coins into a vending machine (“Hey, they’re having in fun in there?” “Oh! Yes, I think they’re onto cake now!”). But most of all, imagine operating with the knowledge that your son or daughter was in the same class as Prince George, and wanting, every night, to ask your Kayla or Jayden, “So . . . are you and George . . . getting along?,” not wanting to make it so obvious to Jayden that, maybe, just maybe, if the cards played out right for these toddlers, George could become his lifetime friend (with fantasies of Jayden giving the best-man speech at George’s wedding, becoming the godfather to George’s child, etc.).

This is all a lengthy preamble to say: for a bunch of parents, this will (sort of) be the case, as Prince George, who will turn three in July, will be attending nursery school, starting at the end of January. Kensington Palace issued the news in a press release this morning, stating that George will be going to Westacre Montessori School Nursery, in Norfolk. The school said, “We are looking forward to welcoming George to our nursery where he will get the same special experience as all of our children.”

CNN notes that, as the school is located near the Duke and Duchess’s Sandringham estate (as opposed to their home in London, at Kensington Palace), the decision indicates that they now think of their country home as “their primary residence” (William’s air-ambulance pilot job is also close to their Sandringham home).

Westacre operates out of a converted chapel and is, again per CNN, “a modest, rural school,” one which costs $49 per day. William also attended a Montessori nursery school when he was a child, though his was located in London, at the private Mrs. Mynors’ Nursery School.

Related: See the Royal Family Christmas Card, Featuring William, Kate, George, and Charlotte
